paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God's people were never meant to run a fan club. The Corinthians were picking teams, Team Paul and Team Apollos, and Paul told them that picking a favorite leader is what "mere men" do (1 Corinthians 3:4). Paul and Apollos are "servants through whom you believed" (1 Corinthians 3:5). "I planted the seed and Apollos watered it, but God made it grow" (1 Corinthians 3:6). I stamp cookies all day and I have never grown a single thing, so I get it. God does the growing, and He gets the credit.

So what do we do with our lives? We build, and we build carefully. There is only one foundation, "which is Jesus Christ" (1 Corinthians 3:11), and everything else gets stacked on top of Him. The Day will test each builder's work with fire, and what lasts will be rewarded (1 Corinthians 3:13-14). Even if someone's work burns up, Paul says he "will be saved, but only as if through the flames" (1 Corinthians 3:15). So the question for you, baker, is not who you follow. It's what you're building on Christ, and whether it's gold or hay.

And here's the part that should make you stand up straight. You are "God's temple," and "God's Spirit dwells in you" (1 Corinthians 3:16). That means you have no reason to chase the wisdom of this world or boast in men, because "All things are yours" (1 Corinthians 3:21-22). Friend, they were fighting over the window seat and Paul told them they own the plane! Then he ends with the best part: "you belong to Christ, and Christ belongs to God" (1 Corinthians 3:23). Paul isn't done with these Corinthians, so keep that oven warm.
